identity: A newspaper/magazine MISCELLANY COLUMN. The first line, من كل بستان زهرة ('a flower from every garden'), is the standing column title — a heading, not prose. What follows is five mutually unrelated short news briefs, one per paragraph: (1) turtles predating/outliving the dinosaurs, (2) internet advertising revenue, (3) the world's third successful hand transplant, (4) African killer ants attacking a Mexican school, (5) pygmy tribes declining in Zaire and Uganda. Register is modern journalistic factual prose — sitting squarely between my doctrine's §A (encyclopedic factual) and §G (popular science / magazine). It is NOT a list, table, MCQ, drill, verse or legal text: there is no enumerated structure anywhere, so the short-tail brake (0b) is IN FORCE throughout and the list rules (H1/I3/J1) are OFF. Six paragraphs, 143 tokens, 6 of them <NL>.
law: One brief per paragraph; inside a brief, ONE INFORMATION CHUNK = ONE UNIT, where a chunk is roughly one finite predication with its own subject/frame (Master Law §0). Because this is factual news prose, the §A/§G cut-laws are live at full strength: و + a conjunct that carries its own predication = CUT (A1/G3), حيث = CUT (A3/G1), بينما = CUT (C2/G1), أي أن(ها) gloss = CUT (C6), and ASYNDETIC continuation that introduces a NEW subject/topic = CUT (A6, and open-contradiction #2's discriminator). Against that, the two brakes that fit a prose genre: (0b) do not strand a <=5-word, non-parallel, dependent-feeling fragment, and (0c) a unit's budget is one-to-two finite clauses, so a SHORT same-subject و-verb rides along rather than opening a unit. و joining BARE nouns/adjectives is never a boundary (conjunct-weight test) — that disposes of والاتصالات/واللاسلكية/والخدمات, ومدرسيها وتلاميذها, وزائير وأوغندا, والحياة الحديثة وأمراضها. Tight subordinators الذي/التي, complementizer أن, and the preposition بسبب never open a unit. Result: 14 units averaging ~10 words, which matches the 5–19-word spread the document itself exhibits.
reasoning: MANDATORY SITES first: 3 (زهرة), 39 (بيضها), 65 (المالية), 93 (العالم), 122 (المستشفى) each sit immediately before an <NL>, and 142 (وأمراضها) is the final token; all six are given. No <NL> token itself carries a boundary. || @17 سنة / أي أنها — CUT, med. C6 (أي إن = CUT, evidenced at doc_8921b794ce19 @667) applies to أي أن(ها) identically: it is the appositive gloss marker, and what follows carries a full finite predication (عاصرت) rather than a bare restatement. Reinforced by 0c: the opening unit أثبتت الدراسات العلمية أن السلاحف ظهرت على كوكب الأرض منذ 200 مليون سنة already spends two finite clauses over 13 words, so its budget is closed before أي arrives. Letting the whole of 5–23 ride would give four finite verbs (أثبتت، ظهرت، عاصرت، انقرضت) in one unit — over budget. || @23 انقرضت / بينما — CUT, med. This is the hardest site in the document and I argued it both ways. AGAINST cutting: بينما ظلت السلاحف تواصل حياتها is exactly 5 words and بينما is grammatically subordinating, which is the profile of my batch-1 false cuts (@811 5 words, @766 5 words); merging it backward would yield a tidy 11-word unit أي أنها عاصرت الديناصورات التي انقرضت بينما ظلت السلاحف تواصل حياتها, two clauses, within budget. FOR cutting, which is what I took: بينما is a table-CUT connective with gold evidence (G1 @484; في حين C2 @200); the clause re-mentions its full lexical subject السلاحف instead of pronominalising, which in this corpus marks a self-contained unit; and the contrast (dinosaurs died / turtles did not) is the entire informational point of the brief, i.e. a genuinely separate chunk under §0. My documented calibration is 7:1 wrong in the merge direction, so a 50/50 site resolves toward the cut. Note also that a 5-word unit is independently attested in this very document (نقل 12 منهم إلى المستشفى). || @28 حياتها / ويخرج — CUT, hi. Textbook A1: و + own subject (صغارها), own finite verb (يخرج), own PP frame (من البيض) and own manner clause (بطريقة تشبه…), 11 words. Conjunct weight is maximal; nothing brakes it. || @55 الماضي / أبرز — CUT, hi. The single clearest boundary here. بلغ دخل … ملياري دولار في العام الماضي is complete; أبرز القطاعات المعلن عنها … opens a brand-new nominal sentence with a brand-new topic and NO connective at all. A6 (asyndetic continuation cuts in factual prose) plus open-contradiction-#2's discriminator (new subject/topic → cut) both fire. || @59 عنها / الكمبيوتر — NO CUT, med. Tempting as an H1 'colon cut': a stem followed by a list, and H1 was my most-repeated batch-1 miss (~35), so checklist item 2 pushes hard for it. I decline, on three grounds. (a) The stem does NOT end mid-construction — أبرز القطاعات المعلن عنها is a complete, well-formed subject NP awaiting its predicate, unlike H1's genuinely dangling ويتضمن الحق في / يتكون … من / تكفل الدولة. (b) The items are three BARE NPs joined by و and riding inline on the same line inside one sentence, with no <NL> between them — that is J5 (المفردات الآتية البيئة الطقس الأوزون, no cuts), not H1, and J5's own discriminator is exactly 'own lines / full clauses → H, bare words inside one sentence → J'. (c) They are conjoined and jointly true, not mutually exclusive answer options, so I2/I3 do not apply either. Cutting would strand a 4-word unit and a 6-word unit in a prose genre where the short-tail brake is live. Same reasoning kills every internal و at 61/63/64 by the plain conjunct-weight test (bare nouns, cf. السمع والبصر والشم). || @77 المفقودة / وذلك — CUT, med. Genuinely uncertain: وذلك has the anaphoric flavour of ولهذا/لذا, which C3 says ATTACH. Three things overturn that. (a) It is not a result connective but a SPECIFICATION connective introducing wholly new information (who the patient was), so it is a new chunk under §0. (b) 7 words with an embedded finite relative (عاش 14 عاما مبتور اليد) clears the 5-word brake. (c) Decisively, وذلك and وتلك at @85 are morphologically PARALLEL openers — E1's 'repeated opening word = repeated boundary', and B2's rule that parallelism defeats the short-tail brake. Also 0c: the preceding unit نجح العلماء في زرع يد جديدة تتحرك … already holds two clauses (نجح، تتحرك) over 11 words, which is precisely the budget-spent condition my C3 caveat used to license the وبذلك cut at doc_8921b794ce19 @1053. || @84 اليد / وتلك — CUT, hi. و + demonstrative subject + copula هي + full predicate, 9 words, and it is a separate summative fact (world ranking of the operation) rather than a continuation of the narrative. A1 straightforwardly. || @105 1956 / واصل — NO CUT, hi. That would sever the subject NP (النمل … الذي وصل … 1956) from its own main verb. الذي/التي never open a unit. || @108 العدوانية / حيث — CUT, hi. حيث is one of my most reliable rules (A3, and G1 fires three times in one doc). The preceding unit is 14 words and complete; هاجم supplies a fresh finite predication. || @112 مكسيكية / وأصاب — NO CUT, med. Default would be A1 CUT, but this is the clearest short-tail/budget case in the document: cutting strands حيث هاجم مدرسة مكسيكية at THREE words — the exact profile of my false cut @594 (وحيرتها فكرة الألمان, 3 words) — and وأصاب العشرات من مدرسيها وتلاميذها is 5 words, same subject (النمل), same event frame (the school attack and its casualties). 0c covers this verbatim: 'short same-subject verbs filling out the same unit's budget' ride along, exactly as ودفعته/فصدر did at doc_3272f207e8c9 @631. The حيث unit as I keep it is 9 words / 2 clauses — a normal size here. || @117 وتلاميذها / نقل — CUT, med. Three finite verbs (هاجم، أصاب، نقل) cannot share one unit under 0c, so a boundary is required somewhere in 110–122, and the choice is between @112 and @117. I take @117 because the break there is ASYNDETIC with a NEW grammatical subject (12 منهم) and a new event (the hospital transfer, a consequence rather than part of the attack), which is the A6 signal, whereas @112 is a mere same-subject و. D2 ('take the earlier candidate') tempted me toward @112 instead, but D2 governs two candidates of the SAME kind; here the later candidate is categorically the stronger one, and the tail نقل 12 منهم إلى المستشفى is an independent passive clause, not a dependent coda. || @134 أعدادها / بسبب — NO CUT, hi. بسبب is a preposition heading a causal PP whose head عجزهم is a verbal noun, not a finite clause; even genuine subordinators (لأن، حتى، إلى أن) never open a unit in this corpus. Paragraph 6 is therefore a single 19-word unit, which the document's own range comfortably admits. || Internal و's ruled bare-noun and left uncut: 61/63/64 (والاتصالات … واللاسلكية … والخدمات), 117 (مدرسيها وتلاميذها — the token still takes a boundary, but for the asyndeton after it, not for its own و), 132 (زائير وأوغندا), 142 (الحياة الحديثة وأمراضها).
